description.text: We are a leading Chinese Smart EV and NEV company that designs, develops, manufactures, and markets Smart EVs and NEVs that primarily appeal to the large and growing base of middle-class consumers in China. We are also expanding our international presence, with a focus on the mid- to high-end segment in the global passenger vehicle market. Since inception, we have taken an innovative technology path to our envisioned future of mobility. We intend to empower consumers with our differentiated Smart EVs and NEVs that can offer disruptive mobility experiences. We believe this can be achieved by fast iteration of software and seamless integration with hardware, which enable us to lead the innovation of Smart EV and NEV technologies and provide differentiated Smart EV and NEV products to consumers. Since our inception in 2015, we have become one of the leading Smart EV and NEV companies in China, with leading software and hardware technology at our core and bringing innovation in advanced driver assistance, smart connectivity and core vehicle systems. We develop full stack advanced driver assistance systems, or ADAS, software in house and have deployed such software on mass-produced vehicles. We started to roll out our XNGP in March 2023 and have made XNGP available in cities without HD map coverage since November 2023. As a result, its geographical coverage has expanded swiftly in China.

about.description_short: XPENG is a leading global Physical AI company, dedicated to bringing artificial intelligence into the physical world to reshape future mobility and smart living. Through in-house R&D, XPENG has developed a full-stack Physical AI architecture spanning Turing AI chips, world foundation models, and highly integrated software and hardware applications. This unified technology foundation powers an expansive product portfolio of smart EVs, robotaxis and humanoid robots, advancing the deployment of Physical AI at scale. Headquartered in Guangzhou, China, XPENG is dual-primary listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. With global capabilities across R&D, manufacturing, sales and services, XPENG drives continuous technological innovation and fosters an open Physical AI ecosystem, making life smarter, safer and better for users worldwide.

analysis_md:
# XPEV — XPeng Inc.
v5 run (engine 5.5.0), 2026-10-20. In scope (market cap $9.073B at $9.53, nasdaq_quote_api; basis: price × shares ÷ ads_ratio).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Guidance, interim-quarter and annual-report figures are from cited search results, as noted.

## What it is
Guangzhou-based Chinese smart-EV maker (SIC 3711, 20-F filer, NYSE: XPEV): battery-electric cars (MONA M03, P7+, P7, G6/G7/G9, X9 including an EREV version) built around an in-house smart-driving stack (XNGP / VLA), the Turing AI chip, and a self-operated fast-charging network, plus high-margin services and other revenue that includes technical R&D services for Volkswagen. Newer bets (humanoid robot IRON, robotics financing in Q2 2026 per search results) are optionality, not yet owner's earnings. Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares — see ADS_RATIO_APPLIED below.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $10,958,647,947.28; net income -$162,760,466.40; operating cash flow $1,179,648,282.36; capex $478,093,621.88 (key_numbers.md capex basis FY2025: PP&E $450.8M + intangibles $27.3M); SBC $80,608,468.68.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $620,946,191.80** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $620.9M, latest FY OE/share $0.65 per ADS). This is the first positive year in the window.
- Maintenance version FY2025: $396,274,552.16 (financials_history.csv, oe_maintenance) — also positive, but below the conservative figure.
- **OE positive 1 of the last 5 fiscal years** (key_numbers.md): the conservative series in financials_history.csv is negative in FY2021 (-$639,490,571.82), FY2022 (-$1,930,262,477.65), FY2023 (-$255,536,551.25) and FY2024 (-$672,534,370.00), then positive in FY2025.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): -$0.29 per ADS** (key_numbers.md: base OE/share $-0.29, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY alone is $0.65 per ADS). The median is the sweep's base by rule, and here it is also the honest one: the latest year is a single inflection year whose operating cash flow was flattered by scale-driven working capital (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE), and the interim 2026 results since then have returned to net losses (search results below). No TTM pin and no base_override were applied — see STALE_FY.
- Balance sheet (engine tags): net debt -$660.0M (key_numbers.md) — i.e. net cash on the cash-and-equivalents tag the engine reads. That understates total liquidity: the company reports a much larger pile once short-term investments and time deposits are included (Q2 2026 cash position RMB40.48 billion as of June 30, 2026, per search results). Shares diluted (latest): 1,903,989,310 ordinary shares (key_numbers.md).

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: Real smart-driving technology differentiation (in-house ADAS/VLA and Turing chip, validated by the Volkswagen partnership) and a large self-operated charging network, but no durable pricing power in a price-war market: vehicle margin was only 12.8% in FY2025, gross margin recovery to 18.9% leans on Volkswagen services revenue, and the ROIC proxy was negative in all of the last 5 fiscal years (-15.8%, -22.9%, -33.0%, -21.2%, -8.5%). A moat of 7+ cannot sit on that ROIC history, so 3/10 (weak).
- Evidence (fundamentals.json, annual): ROIC proxy -15.8% (FY2021), -22.9% (FY2022), -33.0% (FY2023), -21.2% (FY2024), -8.5% (FY2025) — improving, but negative in every year. Gross margin 12.5%, 11.5%, 1.5%, 14.3%, 18.9% over the same years — the FY2023 collapse to 1.5% is what a price war does to a maker without pricing power, and the FY2025 recovery is helped by services mix.
- FOR: In-house ADAS stack (XNGP / VLA) and Turing AI chip — among the leaders in China smart-driving, validated by Volkswagen's technology partnership and R&D-services revenue; Self-operated ultra-fast charging network (3,159 stations at FY2025 per the annual report) supports the brand and ownership experience; Broadened model range (MONA M03, P7+, G7, X9 EREV) drove deliveries +125.9% in FY2025 and overseas expansion is scaling; Technology licensing / services revenue is high-margin and diversifies away from pure vehicle gross profit.
- AGAINST: No pricing power in China's EV price war: vehicle margin only 12.8% in FY2025 despite scale, and buyers switch brands with near-zero cost; ROIC proxy negative in all of the last 5 fiscal years (-33.0% in FY2023 to -8.5% in FY2025, fundamentals.json) — the franchise has never earned above its cost of capital; Scale disadvantage vs BYD and Tesla China in procurement, manufacturing and charging economics; Gross margin is flattered by non-vehicle services (Volkswagen technical R&D services); core vehicle economics remain thin; China consumer / regulatory and VIE/ADS tail risks, plus heavy ongoing AI/robotics R&D spend that must be funded from the car business.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years (key_numbers.md) — academic here, since there is no positive normalized OE stream to fade.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-20)
The final engine pass was run with moat 3 and default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets -12/-5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25), but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the normalized base OE is -$0.29 per ADS, so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F**. F sub-type: no_cash_generation (key_numbers.md: sum of the last 3 fiscal years, the median window, is not positive on OCF - capex).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Price war deepens; FY2025 proves a one-year volume spike | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Deliveries grow but vehicle margin compresses back toward FY2023 | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | Inflection year not yet a run-rate; median OE stays negative | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | FY2025 OE repeats and services/VW revenue keeps compounding | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Sustained positive OE at scale plus robotics monetization | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the growth blend is 61.43% (key_numbers.md components: rev CAGR 5y 65.03%, rev CAGR 3y 41.19%, latest rev YoY 95.74%, OE/share CAGR 2y —). That blend is an inflection artifact of the delivery ramp, not a sustainable start rate — FY2025 deliveries rose 125.9% and revenue 87.7% in RMB terms (annual report, search results), while Q2 2026 revenue growth had already slowed to 8% year over year (search results). Growth is irrelevant to the verdict in any case: it multiplies a negative normalized base. No scenario start was set, and none could rescue a negative base.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): FY2025 deliveries 429,445 (+125.9%), revenue RMB76.72 billion (+87.7%), gross margin 18.9%, net loss RMB1.14 billion, with the first-ever quarterly net profit in Q4 2025. Q2 2026: revenue RMB19.74 billion (+8% YoY, +51.5% QoQ), deliveries 103,295, gross margin 20.7%, vehicle margin 12.1%, net loss RMB1.34 billion; Q3 2026 guidance was deliveries 115,000-121,000 and revenue RMB21.7-23.4 billion. The direction since the FY2025 print is therefore not a clean continuation of the inflection — net losses resumed in H1 2026.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 2025-12-31, 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and cannot compute a TTM for XPEV — it refused with "ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact; shares_diluted: no annual (FY) fact; capex: no capex facts in companyfacts under any candidate tag" (ttm.py reads US-GAAP quarterly facts; XPEV is a 20-F filer with no 10-Q XBRL). No ttm.json exists and no TTM pin was applied; the median base is used and stated as such, per the worker spec for such filers. The interim 6-K was also checked directly for cash-flow legs (the bridged-TTM question): XPeng's Q2 2026 earnings release, furnished on Form 6-K on 2026-08-24, prints unaudited balance sheets, three-month statements of comprehensive loss and GAAP/non-GAAP reconciliations only — it contains no statement of cash flows, so no interim OCF, capex or SBC figures are published from which a bridged TTM could be constructed. The interim evidence that does exist (6-K earnings releases, search results) points the other way anyway: Q2 2026 printed a net loss of RMB1.34 billion after Q4 2025's first profit, so there is no interim basis for claiming a positive TTM OE run-rate in words either.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 3.6%/yr; key_numbers.md share count CAGR 3.59%, growth adj -3.59%): already deducted via the growth adjustment. SBC trend from financials_history.csv: $77,487,801.25 (FY2023), $64,890,735.00 (FY2024), $80,608,468.68 (FY2025) — broadly flat in dollars while revenue roughly doubled over the window, so SBC is shrinking fast as a share of revenue and is not the dilution driver; the count growth is issuance/option-driven and is already charged in the adjustment.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 years): no divestiture, big M&A, or restatement was found in research. The jump is organic volume: FY2025 revenue +87.7% in RMB on deliveries +125.9% (annual report, search results), driven by the MONA M03 / P7+ model ramp. The CAGR inputs are therefore real but inflection-level; they were not used to support any verdict (negative base), and the growth blend is flagged as an artifact in the DCF section above.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): from financials_history.csv — FY2023 net income -$1,460,390,331.25 vs OCF $134,580,083.00; FY2024 net income -$793,266,168.00 vs OCF -$275,690,991.00; FY2025 net income -$162,760,466.40 vs OCF $1,179,648,282.36. OCF runs above net income in all three years: the gap is the normal non-cash addbacks (D&A $231,640,720.00 / $215,330,298.00 / $257,777,348.72 and SBC as above, from financials_history.csv) plus working-capital funding that scales with production as deliveries ramped. No tax-deposit, impairment, or other single one-off explaining the gap was found in research, and none is needed. The consequence for the base is the reverse of a distortion to exploit: FY2025's OCF — and therefore its positive OE — was flattered by that scale-driven working capital, which is a further reason the normalized median, not the latest year alone, is the base.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: reporting currency CNY converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app); flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average, and the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion. Noted — per-share and total figures in this analysis are on that converted basis.
- **USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED**: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency and the engine used the filed USD figures where they exist. Noted; the two FX flags together describe the basis of every dollar figure above.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x2.0 ordinary shares per ADS (XPeng Inc. Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, filed 2026-04-16: the ADSs, each representing two Class A ordinary shares, are listed on NYSE under XPEV; the same ratio is stated in the company's quarterly earnings releases) so they are comparable to the $9.53 ADS price. With the ratio applied, market cap is $9.073B (key_numbers.md, basis: price × shares ÷ ads_ratio); the preliminary run's unscaled $18.164B figure was the per-ordinary-share artifact this flag exists to fix. All per-share figures in this analysis are per ADS.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The FY2025 inflection is real — first positive conservative OE year, first quarterly net profit in Q4 2025, gross margin up to 18.9% — but on this sweep's method it is one year against a negative 3-year median, negative ROIC in all five years, and H1 2026 interim net losses. That is an inflection to verify, not a base to capitalize. Even taking the latest year alone at face value, its OE/share is $0.65 per ADS against a $9.53 price — a thin earnings yield that would need the FY2025 growth rate to persist for years to clear a 15% hurdle, and Q2 2026 revenue growth of 8% YoY says it is not persisting.
- The balance sheet is not the problem: the engine reads net cash of -$660.0M net debt, and the company's reported total liquidity (including short-term investments and time deposits) is materially larger (RMB40.48 billion cash position at June 30, 2026, search results). XPeng can fund several more loss years; whether the car business ever earns its cost of capital is the open question, and the ROIC series says it has not yet.
- Robotics / physical-AI optionality (IRON humanoid, the Q2 2026 robotics financing at a >$6 billion post-money valuation, search results) may be worth something as a sum-of-the-parts matter, but it produces no owner's earnings today and this screen does not capitalize it.
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable from this model — with no positive normalized OE base there is no IV@15% at any price. No tier override: the numbers tier F is retained.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F — no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings; OE DCF not supportable. F sub-type: no_cash_generation)
- Confidence: **Low** (the base rests on a median-vs-inflection-year judgment at a 20-F filer with no buildable TTM, and interim 2026 results are mixed; the F is solid on the filed annual history, but a second consecutive positive OE year would change the picture quickly)
- One-liner: China smart-EV maker at a volume inflection, moat 3/10 — does not clear 15%: Tier F, because normalized (3-yr median) conservative owner's earnings are negative (-$0.29 per ADS; latest FY2025 alone +$0.65 per ADS) after five years of negative ROIC, and H1 2026 interim results returned to net losses; no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
